chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man becomes ritually impure (junub) during the month of Ramadan, then he wakes up, then he sleeps until morning (Fajr).
He said: 'He completes his fast and makes up one other day. And if he did not wake up until morning, his day is complete and it is valid for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if one becomes junub in Ramadan and sleeps until Fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between voluntary and involuntary delay in performing Ghusl during Ramadan, establishing that merely remaining in a state of major impurity (Junub) until Fajr does not invalidate the fast unless accompanied by a conscious decision to delay. The ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on intentionality, where waking up allows for the opportunity to purify oneself, thus requiring a makeup day (Qada) if one chooses to sleep through, whereas sleeping through the wakeful period absolves the individual of the makeup requirement. This nuance is critical in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the validity of the fast and the obligation of expiation (Kaffarah), which applies to deliberate eating or drinking, not merely the state of impurity.
